13.06.02

Finally some real progress: I was able to boot a 'fake kernel' on my BE ! The 'fake kernel' is just the kernel startup code, and a few lines fiddling with the contrast/brightness settings of the LCD, compiled on my linux box with the cross-compile toolchain used to build a real kernel. When I boot it on my BE300 using my modified version of CyaCE (it's in CVS), the screen flickers as expected. so this proves both the bootloader and the toolchain work. (look in the 'Hackers' section if you want to try it yourself)

With respect to the Kernel section for Cassiopeio model E100, could you explain in more detail "needs serial cable to connect". What kind of serial cable is it? How to make the connection -- with a desktop? Are the same cable and mode of connection same as for BE300. Thanks.
 peterkwan (email) - 19.06.02, 14:33

Peter,

you need the Casio serial cable and it is the same cable for both E100 and BE300. The kernel for the E100 is a kernel without framebuffer support, so you won't see anything on the screen. When you connect the serial cable between the E100 and a PC running a terminal program (9600 baud, 8N1), you will see the kernel booting and you'll get a shell prompt.
